title: A message loop, simulated
description:
Run a pretend message loop: post messages, dispatch them, and stop on quit.

```
post WM_CREATE, WM_KEYDOWN 'W', WM_TIMER, WM_CLOSE
dispatch WM_CREATE -> created
dispatch WM_KEYDOWN 'W' -> moving up
dispatch WM_TIMER -> tick 1
dispatch WM_CLOSE -> destroy -> post WM_QUIT
loop ended with exit code 0
```
hints: `std::deque<T>` (from `<deque>`) is a sequence that is cheap to change at both ends, which makes it a natural queue: `push_back(x)` adds at the back, `front()` reads the oldest element, `pop_front()` removes it, and `empty()` says whether any are left.
`WM_CLOSE` leads to `WM_DESTROY`, whose handler posts `WM_QUIT`; that chain is what `DestroyWindow` and `PostQuitMessage` do (lesson 5.05).
Return early from the loop when the message is `WM_QUIT`, with its `wParam` as the exit code.
requirements: A `std::deque` of messages; `postMessage` adds to the back.
A `windowProc` with a `switch` that may post more messages.
The loop stops when it takes `WM_QUIT` off the queue, like `GetMessage` returning 0.
stretch: Add `PeekMessage`-style behaviour: when the queue is empty, run a game frame instead of waiting.
